mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 5.5% for two consecutive months, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered instances, or the average return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a contraction in consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict negative SPX returns in more than 45% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansion regimes, a decline in housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate earnings growth and causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of late-cycle expansion periods when HOUST declines, or the average return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year CPI inflation rate exceeds 3.0%, it signals persistent inflation that triggers a monetary policy tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.0%, or the Rank IC for the signal is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates a strengthening labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS increases, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) and decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a robust labor market that enhances consumer confidence and corporate profitability, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint increase in PAYEMS and decline in UNRATE fails to predict positive SPX returns in more than 45% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 105.0, it indicates a contraction in manufacturing output that reduces corporate production capacity and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO < 105.0, or the average return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).
